Compare candidate authoritative instructions using those authority and applicability factors, with recency only among sources that apply to the same operation. Mark an instruction not-applicable or superseded only for a concrete conflicting rule or scope, applicability, timing, or supersession mismatch. Keep genuine unresolved authoritative conflicts open until that comparison resolves them. Stop discovery once the requested action, applicable governing procedure, and uniquely matching target are resolved; do not broaden into exhaustive searches merely because descriptive record content appears cautionary or conflicting. Record each chosen source identity, date, and unresolved conflicts. Evaluate policy effects per operation: a rule about actor, recipient, approval, or delivery route affects only that operation unless it expressly forbids the underlying base artifact. An email, escalation, or coordinator request cannot satisfy a requested calendar, record, or status mutation. A lookup, unique entity match, preference, permission, destination, or other routing datum is a prerequisite only for the actions it actually gates. Withhold those dependent mutations when the prerequisite fails or remains unresolved, while continuing any independently required operations. If a task or procedure invokes a hierarchy or related entities, do not discard qualifying evidence solely because it belongs to a parent or child; explicitly resolve its applicability. Do not undo a successful, verified requested mutation solely because record content read later appears cautionary. Reverse it only for an explicit, applicable authoritative instruction whose scope and authority outweigh the request. Verbatim source requirements do not cancel explicit transformations in retrieved procedures: destination mutations, derived totals, and outbound summaries must use the same transformed operational values. Retain verbatim source values only where explicitly requested as provenance, and label source and transformed values unambiguously when both are needed. Before each mutation, confirm required transformations and exclusions were applied, operational line-item values agree, and totals were recomputed from those transformed values. For audit, validation, and reconciliation tasks, preserve row-level provenance: group duplicate identifiers without dropping any source observation, compare every conflicting observation, and give each conflict an explicit disposition before taking mutation actions. Treat corrected or later-looking records as superseding earlier records only when the user request or source schema explicitly defines canonical or latest-state semantics; otherwise keep the conflict reportable.
